# 一孔录 Yikonglu (English)

> Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be checked here. Source text, page numbers in the base edition, the commentators' own words, pronunciation, our reading, and a public errata log, arranged book by book and chapter by chapter. Watch the videos on the platforms; come here to check.

## 论语 The Analects
- [1.1 Learning and practising it in season](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/1.html): What you learned, keep taking out to practise and to do. Today: watching the tutorial ten times is watching another bird fly.
- [1.2 Filial and fraternal duty as the root of ren](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/2.html): Filial and fraternal duty is where practising ren begins. Today: kind to strangers online, no patience for one's parents at home — that is starting from the far end.
- [1.3 Clever words and a pleasing face](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/3.html): Watch whether he does it to get the thing done, or only to be liked.
- [1.4 Three things I examine myself on daily](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/4.html): When you act for someone, did you hold anything back? Today: a colleague asks you to look over a plan; you can't be bothered to point out the flaw and say “looks good”.
- [1.5 Governing a state of a thousand chariots](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/5.html): Cheng Yi said these five things sound plain, but pushed to the limit, even Yao and Shun governed no differently. Today: a shop owner keeps every promise made to the staff, doesn't spend carelessly at month's end, and doesn't hand out private errands when people are busiest.
- [1.6 A young man at home is filial](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/6.html): Filial and brotherly duty, care and good faith, love for all come first, study of letters after: this is about order, not choosing one over the other. Today: a very capable person who never reads may do nothing wrong, but the day he does, he has nothing to check himself against.
- [1.7 Honouring the worthy over good looks](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/7.html): Someone who never studied but does all this — Zixia says he has studied. Today: the elders who had only a few years of schooling.
- [1.8 A gentleman without weight has no dignity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/8.html): Zhu Xi takes the words as they stand and does not talk his way around them. Today: the one person willing to tell you to your face tells you twice; if you don't change, the third time he says nothing.
- [1.9 Care at the end, remembrance of the distant](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/9.html): Put your heart into what is easy to overlook and easy to forget. Today: at Qingming someone drives two hundred kilometres just to stand ten minutes at a grave, and goes even though no one is watching.
- [1.10 Whenever the Master arrives in a state](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/10.html): Coming to ask is not the same as handing you the job.
- [1.11 While the father lives, observe the son's intent](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/11.html): Change what is wrong at once; let what can wait, wait. That is time given to what one cannot yet bear to let go. Today: a son inherits his father's small factory. The old rule that cheated customers he scraps the next day; another he never liked he leaves for three years, not because it is right, but because he still can't let it go.
- [1.12 In the use of ritual, harmony is prized](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/12.html): Harmony alone, not regulated by ritual, does not work either. Today: in a team where no one wants to offend anyone, every meeting is all “looks good” and “fine by me”; the meetings are pleasant, and the work drifts further into a mess.
- [1.13 Trust that comes close to what is right](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/13.html): The work of keeping your word happens before you say yes. Today: a friend calls at midnight to borrow money; you say “I'll send it tomorrow,” then hang up, check your balance and panic. Youzi wants you to think in the second before you agree.
- [1.14 A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/14.html): Not going hungry on purpose; simply too occupied to mind.
- [1.15 Poor without flattery](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/15.html): Acknowledge what has been done, then push one step further. Today: from renting to owning without bowing or showing off — Confucius would say “that will do”.
- [1.16 Not troubled that others do not know me](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/16.html): The book opens with “unrecognised and yet not resentful” and closes here; the two ends meet.
- [2.1 Governing by virtue](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/1.html): Not that decrees are unneeded, but that the one who governs must first have gained something himself. Today: a form teacher who means what she says and keeps every promise doesn't need to shout; when the class gets rowdy, the pupils look to her on their own.
- [2.2 Thoughts without crookedness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/2.html): The “without crookedness” lies in the reader, not wholly in the poems. Today: some say novels about villains shouldn't be read; Zhu Xi would disagree: a reader who sees the wrong in them can rein himself in.
- [2.3 Guiding them by decrees](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/3.html): Punishments and decrees keep people from crime; virtue and ritual move them toward good. Today: the estate posts a notice, a 200-yuan fine for dumping rubbish, and the dumping stops; the day the camera breaks, the rubbish comes back.
- [2.4 At fifteen I set my heart on learning](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/4.html): Not a certificate issued automatically at a certain age, but a road of learning.
- [2.5 Meng Yizi asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/5.html): Today: borrowing money to throw a lavish birthday banquet is “doing what one may not”.
- [2.6 Meng Wubo asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/6.html): Parents love their children and fear above all that they fall ill, so children should take their parents' heart as their own and look after their health. Today: staying up all night, drinking, riding without a helmet: you think it's your own business, but on Zhu Xi's reading it is exactly what your parents fear most.
- [2.7 Ziyou asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/7.html): Merely feeding one's parents is no different from keeping dogs and horses; the difference lies in one word, reverence. Today: sending your parents money on time every month, not a cent short, yet on the phone it's always “yes, yes, I know”: the feeding is done, the reverence hasn't kept up.
- [2.8 Zixia asks about filial piety (the hard part is the face)](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/8.html): All the work was done; the face never arrived.
- [2.9 Hui is not slow](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/9.html): Whether someone has learned shows outside the classroom.
- [2.10 Look at what he does](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/10.html): Look at what he does, examine why he does it, see whether his heart is at ease in it. Today: a colleague is always the last to leave and seems hard at work; look closer and he only leaves after the boss does, and the week the boss is away, he's gone at six.
- [2.11 Reviewing the old to know the new](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/11.html): If you can only recite it, reheating it a hundred times still gives the same bowl.
- [2.12 The gentleman is not a vessel](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/12.html): Virtue made whole first, then it can be used anywhere, not learning a hundred trades. Today: an accountant who keeps excellent books has her “vessel”; but when colleagues quarrel or a newcomer slips up, people come to her for advice, and that is more than a vessel.
- [2.13 Act first, then speak](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/13.html): You still speak — only afterwards.
- [2.14 Inclusive, not partisan](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/14.html): Same dishes on the table, different reasons for the dinner.
- [2.15 Learning without thinking](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/15.html): Learning without thinking leaves nothing in the heart: empty (wang). Thinking without learning leaves ideas with nowhere to land: hanging (dai). Today: bookmarking hundreds of online courses and never thinking back on them is wang; reading no books and building a theory of your own that seems truer the more you think is dai.
- [2.16 Working at strange doctrines](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/16.html): Following Zhu Xi: burrowing into it is what does harm.
- [2.17 To know what you know](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/17.html): Admitting you do not know is where it starts.
- [2.18 Zizhang studies to gain office](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/18.html): Confucius promises nothing; he turns seeking office into a lesson in being a person.
- [2.19 Raise up the straight](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/19.html): People submit only when the right people are put to use; the hard part is seeing who is straight. Today: a company promotes the one who only brings good news, while the steady worker who says unwelcome things is left aside; no meeting is needed, everyone below already knows.
- [2.20 Approach them with dignity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/20.html): Ji Kangzi asks for a method; Confucius answers with duty. Treating duty as a method goes wrong again.
- [2.21 Why do you not take part in government?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/21.html): The words are a pretext, and the point is also true.
- [2.22 A person without trustworthiness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/22.html): Without it, the ox is an ox and the cart is a cart; they never connect.
- [2.23 Can ten generations be known?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/23.html): He watched two handovers and saw what stayed and what changed.
- [2.24 Sacrificing to spirits not one's own](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/24.html): Taking gifts to the home of a boss you have nothing to do with; saying nothing in the meeting.
- [3.1 Eight rows of dancers in his courtyard](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/1.html): Four extra rows of dancers measure how hard a heart has become. Today: sitting in the boss's chair at the meeting.
- [3.2 The three families clear away to the Yong](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/2.html): They didn't even understand the song they sang. Today: a corner shop's banner “Welcoming heads of state”.
- [3.3 A person without humaneness — what of ritual?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/3.html): Fill the eight rows, sing the emperor's ode — if the person is wrong, ritual and music can do nothing with him.
- [3.4 Lin Fang asks about the root of ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/4.html): Lavishness and frugality both miss ritual; when both sides are off, lean toward the root. Today: at an elder's birthday, one table is crammed with dishes and everyone stares at their phones; another family has made just a bowl of noodles and sits with the old man until he has finished.
- [3.5 The Yi and Di have rulers](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/5.html): The rebuke is aimed not at the Yi and Di but at his own people. Today: an old family firm where each branch keeps its own books and no one listens to head office; the little shop next door has a single owner and runs in perfect order.
- [3.6 The Ji sacrifice to Mount Tai](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/6.html): Confucius asks Ran You “can you not save him?”: what needed saving was the Ji clan from the guilt of usurping a rite, not Mount Tai's honour. Today: your boss wants to do something against the rules; you work for him, and “I couldn't talk him out of it” lets you off the hook.
- [3.7 The gentleman does not compete](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/7.html): The target does not lie; what is contested is whether your own hand is steady.
- [3.8 The painting comes after the white ground](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/8.html): If the ground is not smooth, every colour you put on comes out blotchy.
- [3.9 Not enough records](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/9.html): Confucius could tell it, but would not rest on his word alone. Today: grandmother's recipe — what's missing is the person standing at the stove.
- [3.10 The di sacrifice after the libation](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/10.html): Looking back, the records and the people are gone; looking around, the rite is there but the heart is not.
- [3.11 Someone asks about the di sacrifice](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/11.html): Saying “I don't know” does not mean he didn't know.
- [3.12 Sacrifice as if present](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/12.html): The form of the rite can be laid out by the book; the heart in it has to be brought by the one who sacrifices.
- [3.13 Better to court the stove](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/13.html): Do the thing right and everyone is easy to deal with; do it wrong and being on good terms with anyone won't help.
- [3.14 Zhou looked to the two dynasties](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/14.html): Following Zhou means following the patient work of watching the forebears improve things bit by bit. Today: at the New Year's Eve dinner a few of grandmother's dishes stay, mother adds two new ones, and the ones too greasy or salty quietly stop being made.
- [3.15 In the Grand Temple he asked about everything](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/15.html): Thirty years in, you still double-check.
- [3.16 In archery, piercing the hide is not the point](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/16.html): The contest is in what can be trained, not in what you were born with.
- [3.17 The sheep for announcing the new moon](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/17.html): The sheep marks the rite; keep the marker and the rite can still be recognised and restored. Today: an old shop that makes one pot of the old recipe at the winter solstice, not for sale.
- [3.18 Serving one's lord with full ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/18.html): Not a bit extra — ritual simply requires this; Confucius says only “people take it for flattery”, with no insult back. Today: getting to the meeting early and filling in expense forms fully, and being mocked as a try-hard.
- [3.19 The lord employs his ministers with ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/19.html): Each side looks only at its own end; Duke Ding was the ruler, and his question was answered with his own half. Today: a team lead first asks whether people are treated with enough respect; the team member first asks whether the work is done properly.
- [3.20 The Guanju: joy without excess](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/20.html): Not too little feeling, but feeling full without going over. Today: crying while reading your wedding vows, wiping your eyes and finishing the last line.
- [3.21 Duke Ai asks about the altar of the soil](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/21.html): The three “nots” are not “never mind” but a heavy rebuke, to make him careful in future. Today: forwarding an unverified message in a group chat — the recall button only works for two minutes.
- [3.22 Guan Zhong's capacity was small](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/22.html): Confucius does not say outright where the smallness lies; it shows in the luxury and usurpation. Today: the company grows, the boss's office becomes a palace, and the rules apply only to others.
- [3.23 The Master speaks of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/23.html): First together, then harmonious, each part clear within the harmony, linked to the end. Today: a choir starts together, then blends, each voice part still audible, singing through in one breath.
- [3.24 The border warden of Yi asks to see him](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/24.html): A minor official saw Confucius's weight at first sight. Today: an old teacher moved off the podium runs free classes in the community, and more people come than were ever in his class.
- [3.25 The Shao is perfectly beautiful and perfectly good](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/25.html): The difference is in how it came: one was yielded, one was taken by force. Today: two equally splendid wins, one earned head-on, one after the opponent withdrew injured — the podium does not taste the same.
- [3.26 High position without generosity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/26.html): It is not that it looks bad; there is nothing left to look at. Today: the man on the phone talking business at the door of the funeral hall — however large his gift, no one remembers he came.
- [4.1 Living among the humane is beautiful](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/1.html): Choose the wrong place to live and what you lose is not the house but the heart that tells right from wrong. Today: when buying a flat people ask about schools, the metro and sunlight, and rarely about how the neighbours treat one another.
- [4.2 The inhumane cannot long endure hardship](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/2.html): Long hardship makes people overstep, long pleasure makes them indulge; whether outside things can take a person away depends on whether the original heart is there. Today: someone out of work for six months still gets up at seven, shaves, and goes out for a run.
- [4.3 Only the humane can love and hate others](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/3.html): Everyone can like and dislike; the “can” lies in doing it rightly, which requires a heart that is not tied to anything. Today: a competition judge who sees a former student take the stage stands up, leaves the panel and gives no score for that round.
- [4.4 Set your heart on humaneness and there is no evil](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/4.html): Resolve does not guarantee no mistakes; it guarantees no intention to do wrong. Today: a learner driver scrapes the car three times in a year but never once runs a red light.
- [4.5 Wealth and rank are what people want](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/5.html): Do not take wealth that should not come, and do not dodge an undeserved poverty by crooked means; the big choices and the small daily work make each other. Today: the bus brakes hard, and the young man's first grab is to steady the old woman beside him.
- [4.6 I have not seen one who loves humaneness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/6.html): Where the heart goes, the strength goes; the hard part is not strength but willingness. Today: the person with no time to exercise scrolls the phone for two hours before bed.
- [4.7 People's faults each follow their kind](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/7.html): Whether a fault leans too generous or too mean shows whether one is humane. Today: two people are half an hour late — one took a fallen old man to hospital, one overslept.
- [4.8 Hear the Way in the morning, die content at dusk](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/8.html): The hard part is not hearing it but truly believing it once heard; only one who has really gained something can say “I could die that evening content.” Today: an old man in a hospital bed finally understands what he never could all his life, holds his daughter's hand and says “now I'm at peace.”
- [4.9 A scholar set on the Way who is ashamed of poor clothes](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/9.html): The mouth says the heart is set on the Way, but the heart is ordered about by things outside. The problem is not dressing poorly; it is treating poor dress as a shame. Today: someone who says he will devote himself to studying for the exam first spends three days picking the most expensive stationery.
- [4.10 No fixed yes, no fixed no; side with what is right](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/10.html): Do not decide in advance and do not refuse in advance; look only at whether it accords with what is right. “Nothing allowed, nothing forbidden” without rightness in charge is mere recklessness. Today: a line judge does not decide beforehand who should win, but bends down to see whether this one ball touched the line.
- [4.11 The gentleman cherishes virtue, the petty man his comfort](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/11.html): “Cherishing one's ground” is not homesickness; it is a heart that guards only its own little comfort. The whole difference between gentleman and petty man lies between public and private. Today: two people receive the same job offer in another city; one asks first what he can learn and whom he can help, the other only which place is more comfortable to stay in.
- [4.12 Act by what profits you, and resentment multiplies](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/12.html): The resentment does not come from the word “profit”; it comes from profiting only oneself. Today: the flatmate who never buys the shared things and uses them most finds no one seeing him off the day he moves out.
- [4.13 Can one govern a state with ritual and yielding?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/13.html): Yielding is the lining inside ritual. When only the outward form is left, ritual itself no longer works, never mind governing a state. Today: a wedding banquet with every seat and formality in order, and the two families quarrel over who sits at the head table until the guests leave.
- [4.14 Worry not about having no post, but about what you stand on](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/14.html): It is not about finding ways to be noticed; it is about first having the substance worth noticing. Whether a post is given, whether others know you, is not in your hands. Today: dozens of résumés with no reply; one person blames the blind employers, another redoes every project in his portfolio.
- [4.15 My Way is threaded through by one](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/15.html): “Loyalty and reciprocity” do not say the Way in full; they hand the learner something to hold. “Threaded through by one” is said only to the one who is ready to understand it. Today: an old craftsman tells the apprentice just one thing: do your own step through to the end, then think of the person who takes over next.
- [4.16 The gentleman understands rightness; the small man understands profit](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/16.html): Both sides use the same kind of “understanding”; the difference is which thing they have understood through and through. Today: someone selling a second-hand item finds a scratch not in the listing, and changes “90% new” to “70% new” on their own.
- [4.17 Seeing a worthy, think of equalling him; seeing an unworthy, look inward](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/17.html): The people one sees are good and bad; each time, fold it back onto oneself. Today: scrolling past a peer's fine work, one person sneers “just luck”, another quietly saves the tutorial.
- [4.18 In serving parents, remonstrate gently](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/18.html): Not keeping silent, but speaking gently, and if it doesn't get through, not falling out, just trying again another time. Today: when parents forward fake ads in the family chat, one child replies “fake again,” another phones them privately and talks it through slowly.
- [4.19 While parents live, do not travel far; if you travel, have a fixed direction](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/19.html): If you can avoid travelling far, do; if you must go, let your parents know where you are. Today: landing on a business trip, first drop a location pin in the family group.
- [4.20 For three years not altering his father's way](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/20.html): The half sentence must be read with the half before it; “do not alter for three years” cannot be taken alone as an iron rule. Today: when young we remember only half of what our parents said, and recall the other half only after running a household ourselves.
- [4.21 One must know the ages of one's parents](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/21.html): Joy and fear are the same fact: one more day lived is one day fewer left. Today: the phone calendar reminds you of a parent's birthday once a year, and the number grows every year.
- [4.22 The ancients did not let words out, ashamed that their conduct would not keep up](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/22.html): The fear is not of saying something wrong but of failing to do it. Today: in the work group chat one person replies “I'll definitely hand it in this week”; another says nothing and hands it in on Wednesday.
- [4.23 Those who err through restraint are few](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/23.html): Holding back words, temper and display are all restraint, not only money. Today: the person who moves house with only two boxes is the one who loses nothing.
- [4.24 The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and quick in action](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/24.html): Of the easy end and the hard end, rein in the easy one (speaking) and spur on the hard one (doing). It is not refusing to speak, but not talking loosely.
- [4.25 Virtue is not solitary; it is sure to have neighbours](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/25.html): This is not “good deeds are rewarded”; it is like answering like. What you hold to draws people who hold to the same thing.
- [4.26 Importune a ruler and you meet disgrace; importune a friend and you grow distant](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/26.html): Persuasion has limits. When it does not get through, stop (with a ruler, leave); urging too often only pushes people away.
- [5.1 Gongye Chang is fit to be given a wife](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/1.html): What matters is that the crime was not his; a prison imposed from outside is no measure of his honour. Today: someone was wrongly disciplined and later cleared; some people avoid him, and some still hand him the important jobs.
- [5.2 Of Zijian the Master said: A gentleman indeed is this man](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/2.html): A person's virtue is taken from the worthies around him, so praising him means also praising those who made him. Today: a newcomer wins an award and the first thing said on stage is to point to a teacher in the audience.
- [5.3 Zigong asked: What about me?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/3.html): Two layers in one line: not yet “not a vessel”, but the most precious kind of vessel; praise with direction in it. Today: the boss says “you're the most useful person on my team”, and it feels good at the time but not quite right on the way home.
- [5.4 Yong is humane but not glib](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/4.html): The root problem is “no real substance”: a quick, argumentative tongue with nothing true in it wins more dislike the more it talks. Confucius did not grant Zhonggong humaneness because humaneness is too great to grant lightly. Today: the person who takes on everything, agrees to everything and delivers nothing finds colleagues walking around him three months later.
- [5.5 The Master wished Qidiao Kai to take office](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/5.html): Whether one's ability is enough, a teacher can see; the hair-thin part not truly gained inside, only oneself knows. Admitting that hair is refusing to rest in small achievement, so Confucius was glad. Today: offered a promotion, she says she can't carry that role yet and asks for another six months.
- [5.6 If the Way does not prevail, I will take a raft out to sea](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/6.html): Going out to sea is a sigh, a figure of speech; Zilu took it literally, with courage to spare but no sense of measuring what is fitting. Today: someone in the group chat says offhand they'll quit and travel the world, and someone else packs a bag that very night.
- [5.7 Meng Wubo asked whether Zilu was humane](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/7.html): Say plainly what visible ability there is; humaneness comes and goes, and one does not vouch for it. Three students, three talents: each line says what they can do, none says they are humane. Today: in a background check, the referee says “I vouch for his skills; his character I can't speak to”.
- [5.8 Who is better, you or Hui?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/8.html): Confucius's question tests whether Zigong sees himself clearly. He does, and does not find it hard to bow, so Confucius first says “you are not his equal” and then solemnly affirms him. Today: a coach asks two players who is stronger, and one points at the other without a second thought.
- [5.9 Zai Yu slept in the daytime](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/9.html): The point is not the nap but a slackened will and words that deeds do not match. “Not worth rebuking” is the heaviest rebuke. Confucius used the occasion to set a rule: hear the words, and also watch the conduct. Today: three gym memberships in a year, and not one visit.
- [5.10 I have never seen anyone who is truly firm](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/10.html): Firmness holds things down; desire is being covered by things. Looking hard and loving to win may mean being led by one's own desires. Today: the person who speaks most aggressively in meetings and yields to no one cannot walk past a mall sale.
- [5.11 What I do not wish others to do to me](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/11.html): The difference is between “not” and “do not”: having no such wish in the first place is ren; having it and holding yourself back is shu. Today: you hate being woken by messages at midnight, so you schedule anything after 10 pm to send the next morning.
- [5.12 The Master's outward cultivation can be heard](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/12.html): “Wenzhang” is virtue showing in words and conduct; Confucius seldom spoke of nature and the Way of Heaven, and Zigong hearing it for the first time is admiration, not complaint. Today: after an apprentice has chopped vegetables in the kitchen for three years, the old chef finally talks to her about heat.
- [5.13 When Zilu heard something](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/13.html): What he feared was not learning more, but the last thing not yet done. His fellow students recorded it because they felt they fell short. Today: one course not yet practised through, so don't sign up for the next.
- [5.14 Why was Kong Wenzi called “wen”?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/14.html): Confucius answers only with the one line of the posthumous-name rules, “quick and fond of learning, not ashamed to ask those below,” without defending Kong Wenzi wholesale. Today: a boss with an ordinary reputation asks the intern in front of everyone, “I don't understand this, can you explain?”
- [5.15 Zichan had four ways of the gentleman](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/15.html): Praising point by point actually shows there is still somewhere he has not reached. Respectful to himself, reverent to superiors, kind to the people, just in employing them: each of the four has its own object. Judging a person by one phrase or one event is wrong. Today: don't judge a small shop open for thirty years by one bad review.
- [5.16 Is it more polite not to stand on ceremony with old friends?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/16.html): Respect fading with time is the usual course; keeping it is what “good at associating with others” means. Today: after five years sharing a flat, a roommate still knocks before borrowing your charger.
- [5.17 Was Zang Wenzhong really clever?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/17.html): Not putting his mind to what the people needed, and courting spirits instead, does not count as wisdom. Today: business is slow, and instead of asking customers, the owner spends a fortune turning the shop door to face another way.
- [5.18 Not even this counts as ren?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/18.html): Loyalty and purity are single virtues; ren asks whether one fully accords with principle and truly has no selfish mind. Trusting small things to vouch for great ones was Zizhang's fault. Today: leaving a job with a clean handover, even the password book left behind, is loyalty to duty — no more than that yet.
- [5.19 Why is thinking twice enough?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/19.html): By the second time it is already clear; by the third, self-interest creeps in. Today: a contract is clear after two readings; by the fourth, you start finding faults that aren't faults.
- [5.20 Why is this “foolishness” harder to learn than cleverness?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/20.html): The “foolishness” is taking on what every clever person avoids, while still keeping himself safe and saving his lord; Master Cheng's mention of Bi Gan shows it is not simply feigning stupidity. Today: the year the company hit trouble everyone left, and she stayed to sort out the bad books.
- [5.21 After so many years of travel, what did Confucius go home to do?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/21.html): He turns from practising the Way to transmitting it; ambitious young men can advance in the Way, but risk overshooting, so he goes home to trim them. Today: a new hire's proposal has eight good ideas in ten pages, and still needs someone to help cut it down.
- [5.22 Bo Yi and Shu Qi were so aloof — why did no one resent them?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/22.html): So fastidious they seemed to tolerate no one, yet they stopped once a person changed, so few resented them; the measure of the pure is not keeping old accounts. Today: the neighbour you once quarrelled with apologised, and you still nod to each other on the stairs.
- [5.23 Why is borrowing something for a neighbour not upright?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/23.html): Saying “I don't have any” is upright; passing off a borrowed thing as your own is bending to please — a small matter, but Master Cheng says what it harms is uprightness itself. Today: a colleague asks for a charging cable, you borrow one from the next desk and say “Here, use mine.”
- [5.24 Why did Confucius find excessive politeness shameful?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/24.html): Both shames are a gap between inside and outside: sweet words, smiles and excessive courtesy to curry favour; befriending someone while nursing a grudge is pretence. Xie says it is worse than theft, because the heart is not upright. Today: holding a grudge, yet being the first at the table to raise a glass to him.
- [5.25 Why was Confucius' wish greater than Zilu's and Yan Yuan's?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/25.html): All three share with others, differing in scale: Zilu shares carriage and horses with friends, Yan Yuan does not boast or show off, Confucius lets each find their place, like heaven and earth nurturing without a trace. Today: the auntie in the housing block whom the elderly trust with their keys and to whose door the children run first after school.
- [5.26 Why is it so hard to see one's own faults?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/26.html): Two levels: knowing one's fault is already rare; knowing it and blaming oneself inwardly is rarer still; only self-arraignment leads to thorough change. Confucius' sigh of “never seen” is a warning to learners. Today: she misreported a figure in a meeting and nobody noticed, and after the meeting she messaged everyone to correct it.
- [5.27 The one thing Confucius claimed to have more of](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/gong-ye-chang/27.html): Loyalty and trust are the base, found everywhere; love of learning is effort, and rare. Confucius does not boast of innate knowledge, only of loving to learn, to encourage others. The Gongye Chang book ends here. Today: honest, reliable people are everywhere; people still going to night school at sixty are few.
- [6.1 Why can one's affairs be simple but not one's heart?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/1.html): With a settled heart and respect in everything, affairs become simple of themselves; aiming first at ease and letting yourself off too is too simple. Today: in the team with the fewest rules, the person in charge is the most punctual and best organised of all.
- [6.2 Why is Confucius' “love of learning” not about reading a lot?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/2.html): Love of learning lies in governing one's feelings: not shifting anger onto others, not making the same mistake twice. Today: scolded at work, you still come home, crouch down, and tie your child's shoelaces properly.
- [6.3 Why did Confucius give one man little grain and another a lot?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/3.html): How much to give depends not on favour but on what is right. Zihua's family rode fat horses and wore light furs, not in need, so he gave only a little, refusing to add to the rich; Yuan Si's salary was owed by his post, and refusing it would be wrong, so any excess should go to his neighbours. One case is “help the needy, not the rich”; the other is “a regular salary should not be declined”.
- [6.4 Can someone of bad background be employed?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/4.html): A calf of a brindled plough-ox, pure red with well-formed horns: even if people will not sacrifice it because of its origin, the spirits of hills and rivers will not reject it. A father's badness cannot cancel a son's goodness; Zhu Xi notes specifically that this speaks about Zhonggong, not to his face.
- [6.5 Where did Yan Hui differ from the others?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/5.html): Yan Hui's humaneness is like a host living at home who now and then steps out; the others' is like a guest who drops by now and then. The difference lies in how long it lasts, not in whether it is there.
- [6.6 Is a single quality enough to take office?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/6.html): Zilu is decisive, Zigong perceptive, Ran Qiu many-skilled: each has one strength and so can be employed. Using people means taking what they are good at.
- [6.7 Offered an office, why would he flee?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/7.html): He would not become the Ji family's retainer, yet he asked the messenger to decline kindly for him, and if they came again he would cross the river to Qi. Neither defying them head-on nor giving in: too hard invites disaster, too soft invites disgrace.
- [6.8 Why did Confucius hold his dying student's hand through the window?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/8.html): Boniu's family moved the sickbed under the south window, as for a ruler's visit; Confucius did not dare accept that honour, so he did not enter and held his hand through the window in farewell. “That such a man should have such an illness” is said twice: grief that such a person should suffer such a disease, laid at the door of fate.
- [6.9 So poor, what was Yan Hui happy about?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/9.html): What he enjoyed was not poverty, but a joy that poverty could not change. Zhu Xi would rather not spell it out, leaving readers to find for themselves what lies in the word “其”.
- [6.10 He said he lacked the strength: why didn't Confucius believe him?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/10.html): Someone truly lacking strength collapses halfway along the road; Ran Qiu drew a line on the ground before setting out. It is not that he cannot, but that he will not.
- [6.11 Both are scholars: where is the difference?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/11.html): Studying the same books, one who learns to make something of himself is a gentleman scholar; one who learns to be seen and to gain advantage is a petty scholar. Profit is not only money; reputation counts too.
- [6.12 Not taking shortcuts: is that talent?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/12.html): He never cut through by-paths and never came to the official's door without public business. Someone who holds firm in small things can be relied on in large ones; Ziyou saw that too when judging people.
- [6.13 He covered the retreat: why wouldn't he admit it?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/13.html): Holding the rear against the enemy in a rout is great merit, yet as they neared the city gate he whipped his horse and said, “It wasn't that I dared to stay behind; the horse wouldn't go.” Passing the credit to his horse shows a heart with no wish to rise above others.
- [6.14 Without a glib tongue or good looks, can one escape trouble?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/14.html): This is not advice to cultivate eloquence and looks; it is a lament for the times: when the world values only a sweet tongue and a pretty face, honest people can hardly escape harm.
- [6.15 Everyone goes out by the door: why not by the right way?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/15.html): Everyone knows to leave by the door rather than climb the wall; the right road in life lies right in front of us, yet people will not take it. It is not that the Way is far from them; they have wandered away themselves.
- [6.16 Too rough or too polished: which would Confucius prefer?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/16.html): Too much plainness is crude, too much ornament is hollow; only the two in balance make a gentleman. If one must lean, better lean plain: with the base intact, refinement can be added; with the base gone, refinement has nowhere to go.
- [6.17 Don't crooked people live perfectly well too?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/17.html): People are meant to live upright; the crooked are alive too, not because they deserve it but because they have got away with it by luck.
- [6.18 Knowing, liking, delighting: what's the difference?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/18.html): Knowing there is this bowl of rice, loving to eat it, and having eaten your fill and being at ease: three levels. The difference is not how much you know, but whether you have actually gained it.
- [6.19 Was Confucius looking down on people?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/19.html): This is not ranking people, but fitting words to the listener: speak too high and the listener cannot catch it, and harm is done. Teach according to capacity, and climb step by step.
- [6.20 Did Confucius believe in spirits?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/yong-ye/20.html): The question is not belief or disbelief, but revering and keeping at a distance: first do fully what human affairs require, revere the spirits without petitioning them; in action, the hard part first and the gain after, without reckoning the benefit in advance.
